title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: PLAC courtier sons lose goods; tip — impute to unborn?
pass_a_gloss: Further: when the courtier loses titles, dignities, and estates, his sons lose them too, and the father's unfaithfulness harms them. Placeus grants Adam's fall harmed us vehemently—we are begotten deprived as he was of justice and rectitude. But does a judge impute the courtier's crime to sons yet unborn and to grandsons? Tip before GAR's Denique on parental crime descending.
pass_b_english: Besides, when the Courtier is deprived of titles, dignities, and estates, his sons are deprived of the same, and the father's unfaithfulness harms them. I also confess that Adam's fall harmed us, and indeed vehemently, and that as he was deprived of justice and rectitude, so we are begotten by him deprived of the same. But do you think the Courtier's crime is imputed by the judge to his sons yet to be born and to his grandsons?
source_text: Praeterea privato Aulico titulis, dignitatibus & fundis, iisdem privantur eius filii, & nocet iis patris infidelitas. Confiteor etiam lapsum Adami nobis obfuisse & quidem vehementer, & quam ille fuit privatus justitia & rectitudine tam iisdem nos privatos ab eo gigni. Sed putasne crimen Aulici imputari a judice eius filiis nascituris & nepotibus?
